requirements.requirement: Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped as Primary/Synced with wsrep_cluster_size=1 (cmd-2aeb935153744995), appdb.orders created and seeded (cmd-3d360ca65c184443). node2 joined via rsync SST and reached Synced state with the seeded rows present (cmd-6681b74c105b45a1). node3 subsequently joined via SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, with all rows intact (cmd-e2c2ab5de179457d). A cross-node write/read check (cmd-7be4cb03becb404e / cmd-1fc95a689f1d4918) confirms multi-master replication among the three original members.

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth member carrying data that already exists in the cluster
requirements.summary: node4 was initialized, started, and performed a full SST, joining at wsrep_cluster_size=4 with local_state Synced; the select immediately after shows all pre-existing rows (widget/gadget/gizmo/doohickey) present on node4 (cmd-8c0849752c5840a8). node1's incoming-addresses list also confirms 4 distinct members (cmd-4796ca99c8f641e3).

requirements.requirement: node4 should accept writes like the other members
requirements.summary: An insert issued directly on node4 (thingamajig) is visible on node4 itself and immediately visible on node1 with wsrep_cluster_size=4 (cmd-b7a44c7e373a414e, cmd-4796ca99c8f641e3). A later insert on node2 after the full restart cycle is likewise visible on node4 (cmd-236d8ed3958e41b5, cmd-2ecdeb0b6454443c), confirming bidirectional multi-master behavior including node4.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol across all 4 managed nodes (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: For each node, a baseline boot_id and healthy Synced/Primary/cluster_size=4 state was captured (cmd-13e1230187624fab, cmd-73104e0f467f4580, cmd-40a86b5d9c54433d, cmd-0816e3d3e6854c82) immediately before a native reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-c2d26894ece647e9, cmd-5aaad95f0f6e41aa, cmd-4afef5e4cf7e4318, cmd-19cc78b0ff004bb9). After a bounded series of expected connection failures during reboot, each node reconnected with a distinct new boot_id (cmd-0a660bd25d3642e0, cmd-3fee775f2ca841c9, cmd-bbc4b7c3fd1143df, cmd-0029a8b895174afc), and mariadb auto-started and rejoined at cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced with all rows intact (cmd-5218e2375a904735, cmd-e79f288372014f73, cmd-7610612be0b14054, cmd-bebae837d5c04b6f). The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot boot-identity values (5adae18f/747834de/49425a3c/e01c418a for node1-4) match the executor's final observed boot ids exactly, corroborating the restart evidence independently. A final post-restart write on node2 propagated correctly to node4 (cmd-236d8ed3958e41b5, cmd-2ecdeb0b6454443c).

overall_summary: The executor delivered a functioning 4-node MariaDB Galera cluster: node1-node3 formed the initial cluster and held seeded application data, node4 was subsequently added and received the existing data via full SST, and both node4 and the original members demonstrably accept and propagate writes across the whole cluster (verified before and after a full restart cycle). The mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on all four nodes with baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full cluster/data recovery, and this is independently corroborated by the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot boot-identity values matching the executor's own observations. The path to this end state involved a large number of failed/corrective commands (crashed mariadbd starts, non-primary views, an Alpine BusyBox ps/lsof incompatibility that blocked SST) but these were all legitimate troubleshooting toward the final working state and left no problematic residue.
limitations: A large fraction of executor commands (53 of 177 failed) reflect an unusually long trial-and-error bootstrap process; while each failure was diagnosed and corrected, this reduces confidence slightly in whether the final configuration is the cleanest possible steady-state versus an artifact of repeated patching.

Root credentials for the mariadb 'root' user were used throughout with no password set; this is standard for a lab/test cluster but was not evaluated against any explicit security requirement since none was stated in the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor went through a long, messy bootstrap process on node1/node2/node3 with many failed mariadbd starts, crashed states, and repeated wipes of /var/lib/mysql (e.g. cmd-844c40c342a84a07, cmd-d1dfba64d09f488c, cmd-936525384d264564, cmd-29b18502ea564f15, cmd-9433acc8e8e14726, cmd-f12d6de06d864da4). These were all corrective actions responding to earlier failed bootstrap/join attempts (wrong command_args, stale pid/socket files, non-primary views, the BusyBox ps/lsof SST incompatibility) rather than unrelated troubleshooting experiments, and each wipe was followed by a successful re-initialization that produced the final working state — none left residue since the data directories were fully repopulated via install-db + bootstrap/SST. The apk installs of procps and lsof (cmd-f4b3d9fbc1664e1e-family, cmd-0160192000a84664, cmd-3ac5441b44624718, cmd-34cd8ec3327e4ee8, cmd-cd173eee6d794a94) were a necessary and retained fix for a genuine platform bug blocking SST, applied uniformly to all four nodes. The start_pre() edit to /etc/init.d/mariadb (cmd-010f0d604a4140c4 and per-node equivalents) and rc-update add mariadb default were required for boot persistence, matching the mandatory restart-recovery requirement, and remained in place with no adverse effect (after_executor shows mariadbd correctly listening on 3306/4567 on all nodes, no failed/crashed services). The one leftover artifact is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log per node from the 'nohup reboot' invocations, which is negligible. Package-health diffs are unchanged from baseline (pre-existing chrony.drift only). No unsafe exposure, no conflicting services, and no unnecessary retained mutations beyond what the task and its bounded restart protocol required.
